title: APO Fennel and Yukon Gold Gratin
description: Thin potato and fennel slices soften together in a nutmeg-scented milk sauce with Gruyère.
equipment: Anova Precision Oven Gen 1 with food probe and bottom drip pan

ingredients.name: trimmed fresh fennel bulb
ingredients.note: Remove the core and slice paper thin across the fibers.

steps.title: Preheat the APO
steps.text: Install the bottom drip pan and set the APO to 335°F, sous vide mode off, 60% steam, rear element on, top and bottom off.

steps.title: Start the roux
steps.text: Whisk {butter} and {flour} together in a small saucepan over medium-low heat for 1 minute.

steps.title: Make the milk sauce
steps.text: Gradually whisk {milk} and {nutmeg} into the roux and simmer for 2 minutes, until the sauce coats a spoon.

steps.title: Layer the vegetables
steps.text: Alternate overlapping layers of {potatoes} and {fennel} in the dish, spooning sauce between the layers and over the top.

steps.title: Add the cheese
steps.text: Scatter {cheese} evenly over the sauced surface.

steps.title: Steam-bake the gratin
steps.text: Insert the probe at an angle into the middle layers, clear of the dish, and set its target to 200°F. Bake for 40–55 minutes until the target is reached and a thin knife slides through the potatoes. If still firm, keep baking in 3-minute intervals.

steps.title: Let the sauce settle
steps.text: Rest for 5 minutes before spooning the gratin and its sauce onto two plates.

notes: Make ahead: Slice the fennel a day ahead and keep it covered in the refrigerator. Slice the potatoes just before assembly. Refrigerate in shallow portions within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: No. The thin potato slices can turn grainy and the milk sauce can separate. Fridge reheat: Set the APO with the drip pan installed to 325°F, sous vide mode off, 60% steam, rear element on, top and bottom off. Put a portion in a covered shallow dish with a splash of milk and start checking after 12 minutes. Check for 165°F in the center with the food probe or an instant-read thermometer. Freezer reheat: Thaw in the refrigerator overnight, then follow the fridge reheat instructions. For dairy-free gratin, use plain unsweetened oat milk and neutral oil in the sauce and omit the Gruyère. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/2 of recipe): 233 kcal, 9.8 g protein, 32.9 g total carbohydrate, 7.6 g fat, 3.1 g fiber, 144 mg sodium.
